decisions.why: This implements 'owing nothing' as the task states it. Leaving the fingerprint rule unchanged avoids moving every pop-up's fingerprint, which would itself be a cascade.

decisions.summary: A pop-up that is not answered as it stands is not edited. It is named, and its owed check makes the link as a LINKS fix. The writer runs after modal-triage's own clears so that this set is as small as it can be.
decisions.why: The task says the split adds the target to EACH such pop-up, mechanically and owing nothing. Following the literal reading there would defeat the request's stated purpose. The carve-out does not empty the rule: the link is still made, by the check the pop-up already owes (now bound by the new D5/LINKS clause), and the pop-up is named rather than skipped silently. It covers exactly one class: pop-ups that already owe a check.

Two knobs, measured 2026-11-25 over 52 (pop-up, target) pairs; they select exactly the two pairs that state the moved sections, as read by eye.
decisions.why: The task requires a test for 'states', and this is that test, with its thresholds measured against the whole tree and checked by eye. decisions.summary: the round arbiter accepted T235's section as it stands
`which` kept in ASK only as the interrogative (`which (one |of these|...)?(do you|would you|should I|shall I)`)
decisions.why: The task is to stop statements firing as asks (the task line, and the GM's 2026-11-25 question about efficiencies in the check). On the corpus this alternative fired on 18 F (relative clauses) and on no T that another alternative missed, so no ask is lost; the interrogative form is kept.

decisions.summary: A STATED decision (`your call`, `needs your ...`, `ask you`, `waiting on you`, ...) is exempt when `nothing`/`none`/`nobody`/`neither`/`no one` stands earlier in its clause, or `not`/`never`/`-n't` within two words before it
decisions.why: Exempting a negated statement (`Nothing is waiting on you`, `didn't ask you anything`) serves the purpose: the GM asked for efficiencies and each false firing costs an escalation-check run. But the bound as written also exempts ordinary asks, which feature 429 FR-002 says are refused and which this section's own goal (item 1) and its Recall paragraph say still fire. The `-n't` within-two-words window exempts `This can't land without your call.` (can't [land without] your call). The clause-wide `nothing` exempts `Nothing else needs your decision except the budget.` and `Nothing is left but your call on the split.` The old rule refused all three. A tighter bound is possible: the negation governs the stated phrase itself, with no `without`/`until`/`unless`/`but`/`except` between them. So the case is not impossible, it is not implied by the GM's words, and the literal rule does not defeat the purpose. The corpus shows no real T lost, but round 1 judged the same way on a constructed form (`Waiting on your go-ahead to land it.`). Fix: tighten the bound, and pin these forms as asks in the new test.

decisions.summary: A STATED decision after `of` or `spent` (`442 minutes of waiting on you`, `the time spent waiting on you`) is a measure, not an ask
decisions.why: These are reports of time, and they fired on corpus F messages. `of`/`spent` immediately before the phrase does not reach a decision put to him in any ordinary form, so the bound holds to its purpose: stopping statements from costing a check run, as the GM asked on 2026-11-25.

decisions.summary: A sentence-opening `waiting ...` is a measure's name when it is the subject of is/was/were, or when it is a table cell with no `:`
decisions.why: Judged in two parts. (a) The subject of is/was/were (`**Waiting on you** is still reported`) is a measure's name. That part is LEGITIMATE on its own and is bounded. (b) 'A table cell with no `:`' reaches past measure names to status rows. `| T26 | Waiting on your budget answer |` and `| T22 | Waiting on your go-ahead |` are exempted. In sentence form this section itself treats them as asks or borderline-kept (`T26 is still waiting on your budget answer` stays firing; `Waiting on your go-ahead to land it.` fires). The pinned table ask has a colon, so the test does not reach this form. A tighter bound exists: the row's first cell, or a cell followed by a numeric cell, as in the measure example `| Waiting for you to answer | 0.5 | 1% |`. Fix: bound (b) so that a status cell still fires, and pin a no-colon status cell as an ask.

decisions.summary: OFFER gains `if you agree` and a sentence opening `Say if`
decisions.why: This adds refusals and removes none. It enforces feature 429 amendment 1's rule that an offer owes the filter, so it is enforcement of what was asked, not unrequested scope. Measured over 6,374 end-of-turn messages: 28 new firings, each an offer on reading. Amendment 1's text is not in the bundle (spec-cited.md carries only 429 FR-002 and 375 FR-044), so this ruling rests on the block's citation of it.

decisions.summary: The 8 borderline firings stay firing
decisions.why: No change to them. Each puts something to the GM (a pointer to a question, a deferred decision, a pause for his word, an invitation), so they keep firing under FR-002. The feature-432 kept-id exemption is unchanged. Feature 432's text is not in the bundle, so this rests on the block's citation of it.

decisions.summary: A narrower prompt to escalation-check (only the flagged sentences, not the draft) is not built
decisions.why: The GM's words ask whether more efficient ways exist and do not request this lever. The session's own reply named the narrower bundle as a separate change. Leaving it out drops nothing the GM asked for in T235.

decisions.summary: A strict '?'-or-offer detector is not adopted
decisions.why: The '?'-or-offer wording is the session's sketch, not the GM's words. The sketch's purpose is that only messages putting something to him reach the agent, and the plan's rule implements that purpose. The literal form would drop 24 of the 74 true asks on the corpus (measured 2026-11-25), contrary to feature 429 FR-002. Even read as a narrowing of the relayed brief, it would be LEGITIMATE, because the literal rule defeats the check's purpose.

decisions.summary: The 112-message labeled corpus stays in the session scratchpad, not the repository; the task's named statements are the committed cases
decisions.why: FR-002 asks for the detector's hit rate, a sample of hits and recall to be recorded, not for the raw messages to be committed. The section records the figures (with date and method) and quotes a sample of the forms, and the repository is public.

decisions.summary: `Performance work? no`
decisions.why: This label decides only scheduling under FR-013, and the task is being done now, so no ordering the GM asked for is lost. It arguably undersells the work: each false firing avoided saves an escalation-check run and a turn, which is the efficiency the GM's 2026-11-25 words ask about. That is not a narrowing of what is built.

blocks: ### T232 (the 2026-11-24 landing: modal-research passed sheet/guest-quarters in the morning and found the alcove gap in the afternoon on one fingerprint, the fix re-owing a depiction check; claims-triage sent 5 then 2 of 44 claims on)

decisions.summary: Route (1) is not built: an answered unit on an unchanged fingerprint is already not re-owed (make record-owed).
decisions.why: Nothing changes, and the block says why: the incident's re-run was forced by an arbiter ruling, not owed by the tool.

decisions.why: This is a design choice between routes the brief offered. It drops nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.why: Measurement method. The block states the reason, which is measured (2 to 10 minutes apart, counts falling).

decisions.why: The finding is measured and leaves no defect: the two bundles differed. The block states this rather than assuming variance.

decisions.summary: make record-checked marks an answer at a fingerprint the unit was already answered at (rerun: the fingerprint and the earlier result). The answer is still recorded and re-stamps the build. The mark clears with the next answer or settle at another fingerprint.
decisions.why: Bookkeeping that makes a re-run visible. The forced re-run still does its job of re-stamping the build. A test enforces it.

decisions.summary: Route (2), for text an earlier round judged and passed: a re-run's new EDIT on a pop-up whose text that answer stood on is held and kept in noted.jsonl, not applied mid-landing. RERUN_OK applies it. A dry run holds nothing.
decisions.why: This is implied by the GM's own words: 'settled choices stay settled' and 're-reviews scoped to the change' (the seven rules he approved on 2026-11-23), and on the cascade, 'cascading set of changes that is mostly not finding actual problems ... we have to fix that before we move forward.' The sheet/barracks case is this class: a scoped round 6, then a re-run that raised a different NOTE on a paragraph earlier rounds had passed, with two EDITs. Holding that re-litigation serves the request's purpose.

decisions.summary: The hold makes no distinction between a factual correction and a style note. It keys on the unit's fingerprint, not on what the earlier round covered. So a factual EDIT on text the earlier round never opened is held as a noted.jsonl row too: the incident's own alcove gap, which the morning round said it 'did not re-open' and which the GM's commit 1b064aa0de landed. The block says this costs 'one session's delay'. But its own constraint line says such notes are 'listed and kept, never filed or applied' (451 T219, T229), and the only route it names for applying one is the RERUN_OK bypass.
decisions.why: Judged on its purpose, not its wording. The GM separated factual findings from style: 'style edits are just a different category of thing than factual inaccuracies ... when we are cascading, we are only interested in factual inaccuracies'. He approved 'only factual findings cascade' and asked on 2026-11-24 that 'we really are cascading in situations that do call for it.' 'Settled choices stay settled' protects judgment calls that were made, not a factual gap in text no round opened. Run through this tool, the incident's valid finding ends as a never-applied note. The block's 'one session's delay' names no mechanism that delivers it, so the decision does not do what it says. That also cuts against 'fix defects where you find them' (constitution XIV), which the block cites as a constraint. One argument is stretched over two unlike things: a style re-litigation and a factual correction. To pass, the block must do one of two things. (i) Name the route by which a held factual EDIT is applied: a target the next session runs, or each one filed as a task ordered before the next step, with a test that a held EDIT reaches it. Or (ii) not hold an EDIT that corrects a factual error (or a GUESS/attested label), so the hold covers only re-litigated notes and wording. The cause of the morning miss (no line saying what a round covers) is deferred to T249 while this hold lands first. That deferral is why the hold must not, meanwhile, swallow the factual findings that miss produces.

decisions.summary: apply-edits holds every EDIT on a pop-up file whose unit carries rerun at its current fingerprint 'for any of the reply's checks'. A reply that mixes a re-run check with a first-round check therefore has the first-round check's EDITs held as well.
decisions.why: Taken on its own, this reach is outside even the rule that justifies the hold. A check answering a fingerprint for the first time has had no earlier round pass that text, so 'what an earlier round passed stays passed' cannot apply to its findings. Nothing in the GM's words settles text that no round of that check judged. The block must hold only the EDITs of a check that is itself a re-run at that fingerprint. Alternatively it must state, measured, that a reply never mixes a re-run check with a first-round one, or that its EDITs cannot be attributed and why holding all of them is still confined to re-judged text.

decisions.summary: Found and fixed here: the measurement's replay overwrote sheet/guest-quarters' kept round-5 snapshot, which produced a false change section. The snapshot is restored to the text that round judged, and a rebuilt bundle shows no change section.
decisions.why: A defect found and fixed in the task (constitution XIV, fix as we go).

decisions.summary: A re-run of a record check on a research page is not held. This is filed as T249 and lands before T246.
decisions.why: This is not a wrong outcome. The EDITs are findings, and applying them costs re-owed checks but changes no map or verdict wrongly. No record-check re-runs on pages have been measured. The deferral carries FR-009's three parts: why, filed id, order.

decisions.summary: When a subject's last round predates the kept snapshots, a later round gets no change section and no line saying what it covers. This is filed as T249 and lands before T246, because bundle::earlier lies outside this task's hold.
decisions.why: This is a real defect by the project's definition: a round passed text it never opened and missed the alcove gap. The deferral alone stays within because it carries FR-009's why, filed id and order inside the feature, and the bundle does not show that T246 is a later port step. T249 must land before the next port step (fix as we go). Its interaction with the hold is ruled under hold-factual-finding-with-no-route. Note too that the block rejects route (3) as 'another line would repeat it', while T249's fix is itself a bundle line.

decisions.summary: 'Performance work? no.'
decisions.why: A declaration. Nothing is decided against the request.

For a pop-up that already owes a check, those two clauses conflict: the edit would turn the triage it is owed into a full check, so the split would cause more owing, against 'owing nothing' and against the GM's 'nothing needs to cascade simply because a split occurs'. The carve-out does not empty the rule: the link is still made, by the check the pop-up already owes (now bound by the new D5/LINKS clause), and the pop-up is named rather than skipped silently. It covers exactly one class: pop-ups that already owe a check.

blocks: ### T235 (the Stop hook's QUESTION UNFILTERED fired on statements, `Nothing is waiting on you.` and `That lets you see, for example, whether ...` among them, each costing an escalation-check run that kept the reply as information; the GM asked 2026-11-25 for efficiencies in that check (request.md, "the escalation check's cost"), and the session's reply named a mechanical pre-filter as T235's shape)

decisions.summary: `which` kept in ASK only as the interrogative (`which (one |of these|...)?(do you|would you|should I|shall I)`)
decisions.why: The task is to stop statements firing as asks (the task line, and the GM's 2026-11-25 question about efficiencies in the check). On the corpus this alternative fired on 18 F (relative clauses) and on no T that another alternative missed, so no ask is lost; the interrogative form is kept.

decisions.summary: A STATED decision (`your call`, `needs your ...`, `ask you`, `waiting on you`, ...) is exempt when `nothing`/`none`/`nobody`/`neither`/`no one` stands earlier in its clause, or `not`/`never`/`-n't` within two words before it
decisions.why: Exempting a negated statement (`Nothing is waiting on you`, `didn't ask you anything`) serves the purpose: the GM asked for efficiencies and each false firing costs an escalation-check run. But the bound as written also exempts ordinary asks, which feature 429 FR-002 says are refused and which this section's own goal (item 1) and its Recall paragraph say still fire. The `-n't` within-two-words window exempts `This can't land without your call.` (can't [land without] your call). The clause-wide `nothing` exempts `Nothing else needs your decision except the budget.` and `Nothing is left but your call on the split.` The old rule refused all three. A tighter bound is possible: the negation governs the stated phrase itself, with no `without`/`until`/`unless`/`but`/`except` between them. So the case is not impossible, it is not implied by the GM's words, and the literal rule does not defeat the purpose. The corpus shows no real T lost, but round 1 judged the same way on a constructed form (`Waiting on your go-ahead to land it.`). Fix: tighten the bound, and pin these forms as asks in the new test.

decisions.summary: A STATED decision after `of` or `spent` (`442 minutes of waiting on you`, `the time spent waiting on you`) is a measure, not an ask
decisions.why: These are reports of time, and they fired on corpus F messages. `of`/`spent` immediately before the phrase does not reach a decision put to him in any ordinary form, so the bound holds to its purpose: stopping statements from costing a check run, as the GM asked on 2026-11-25.

decisions.summary: A sentence-opening `waiting ...` is a measure's name when it is the subject of is/was/were, or when it is a table cell with no `:`
decisions.why: Judged in two parts. (a) The subject of is/was/were (`**Waiting on you** is still reported`) is a measure's name. That part is LEGITIMATE on its own and is bounded. (b) 'A table cell with no `:`' reaches past measure names to status rows. `| T26 | Waiting on your budget answer |` and `| T22 | Waiting on your go-ahead |` are exempted. In sentence form this section itself treats them as asks or borderline-kept (`T26 is still waiting on your budget answer` stays firing; `Waiting on your go-ahead to land it.` fires). The pinned table ask has a colon, so the test does not reach this form. A tighter bound exists: the row's first cell, or a cell followed by a numeric cell, as in the measure example `| Waiting for you to answer | 0.5 | 1% |`. Fix: bound (b) so that a status cell still fires, and pin a no-colon status cell as an ask.

decisions.summary: OFFER gains `if you agree` and a sentence opening `Say if`
decisions.why: This adds refusals and removes none. It enforces feature 429 amendment 1's rule that an offer owes the filter, so it is enforcement of what was asked, not unrequested scope. Measured over 6,374 end-of-turn messages: 28 new firings, each an offer on reading. Amendment 1's text is not in the bundle (spec-cited.md carries only 429 FR-002 and 375 FR-044), so this ruling rests on the block's citation of it.

decisions.summary: The 8 borderline firings stay firing
decisions.why: No change to them. Each puts something to the GM (a pointer to a question, a deferred decision, a pause for his word, an invitation), so they keep firing under FR-002. The feature-432 kept-id exemption is unchanged. Feature 432's text is not in the bundle, so this rests on the block's citation of it.

decisions.summary: A narrower prompt to escalation-check (only the flagged sentences, not the draft) is not built
decisions.why: The GM's words ask whether more efficient ways exist and do not request this lever. The session's own reply named the narrower bundle as a separate change. Leaving it out drops nothing the GM asked for in T235.

decisions.summary: A strict '?'-or-offer detector is not adopted
decisions.why: The '?'-or-offer wording is the session's sketch, not the GM's words. The sketch's purpose is that only messages putting something to him reach the agent, and the plan's rule implements that purpose. The literal form would drop 24 of the 74 true asks on the corpus (measured 2026-11-25), contrary to feature 429 FR-002. Even read as a narrowing of the relayed brief, it would be LEGITIMATE, because the literal rule defeats the check's purpose.

decisions.summary: The 112-message labeled corpus stays in the session scratchpad, not the repository; the task's named statements are the committed cases
decisions.why: FR-002 asks for the detector's hit rate, a sample of hits and recall to be recorded, not for the raw messages to be committed. The section records the figures (with date and method) and quotes a sample of the forms, and the repository is public.

decisions.summary: `Performance work? no`
decisions.why: This label decides only scheduling under FR-013, and the task is being done now, so no ordering the GM asked for is lost. It arguably undersells the work: each false firing avoided saves an escalation-check run and a turn, which is the efficiency the GM's 2026-11-25 words ask about. That is not a narrowing of what is built.
